title: Full audit of mhfe 0.8.0: generation removed, own signal handling, reproducible macOS archives

reviewer.name: Coordinator with two reviewers: A library, command line, signal handling and xtask; B documents, build and release, browser package

snapshot.workingTree: uncommitted changes on v0.7.0, diff against HEAD with SHA-256 b6fe7ad7e8644e1b29e8807c473c53a1f8ffc552093055398ac72b873d283a6b (404851 bytes), the new xtask/src/macho.rs included as intent-to-add

scope: Every change after v0.7.0 (8a15bed), all in the uncommitted working tree of 0.8.0: seed-phrase generation removed (mhfe new, chosen words, the draw of the wallet check, the browser package's drawPhrase and describeDraw, the wallet module's random source and two error codes), an own Unix handler of Ctrl+C, SIGTERM and SIGHUP instead of ctrlc, reproducible macOS archives linked by Zig in the canonical build with cargo xtask macos-binary, the release workflow's macOS job, and the documents. All 32 CHECK items were assigned; code that did not change was not reviewed again.

coverage.evidence: PhraseDraw, NewPhrase, drawPhrase, describeDraw and the secret fields passphraseRepeat and chosenWords left together; no new copy of a secret. The stop thread ends the process through hidden_input::restore_and_exit, as ctrlc's thread did.
The worker operation allowlist, both SECRET_FIELDS lists and WORKER_NEWS drop the draw in step; MhfeWallet no longer declares needs random; no network API or remote resource added.
No network code changed; both ends of the stop pipe are close-on-exec, so a program the tool starts inherits neither, and exec resets the caught handlers.
Only the passwords module still draws, through check_source and uniform_below; the wallet module takes no source. The gates left for browser-wallet reach no production draw (AUD-048-ARC003).

Error paths of on_stop_signals: a failed pipe, fcntl or thread leaves the default handlers and prints the note; a signal before the reader runs waits in the pipe; EINTR is retried; a full pipe drops the byte without blocking. The terminal suite passed Ctrl+C, SIGTERM, Ctrl+\ and Ctrl+Z under isolation.
No added line under web/ or xtask/pages holds innerHTML, eval, Function, storage, fetch, a dynamic import or console output.
AUD-048-BLD001: the Mach-O tool bounds its word reads but not its page loop.
wallet_check::verify still refuses an empty passphrase and any length but 24 words; the known answers keep the four published digests and the refusal without a passphrase.
src/wallet.rs and the derivation code are not in the diff; the wallet set keeps its keys, addresses, address-search and wallet-check parts.
No provider or network lookup in mhfe.
No transaction building or signing in mhfe.
No wallet discovery or balance scanning in mhfe.
Only the creation side of MHFE-WALLET-CHECK-SEED-1 left; recovery, rehearsal, search and decrypt evaluate the 16-bit check through wallet_check::verify; container formats untouched.
No public-data viewer or provider aggregation in mhfe.
The worker calls selfCheckWallet(tier, skip, onStart, onResult) as the binding takes it; the package checks' stand-in does not (AUD-048-ARC002).
MhfeWallet lost its operation slot and cancel() with its only long operation; its calls are one-shot workers that wait for the startup check.
walletParameters {version, coins, walletCheckBits} matches wallet.d.ts and the documents; MhfeErrorCode drops the two codes as src/error.rs does.
The wallet bindings still take UTF-8 bytes through SecretText; the Mach-O tool reads the header, LC_UUID, LC_CODE_SIGNATURE, superblob and code directory at the right offsets.
mhfe ships no HTML interface of its own; host pages supply it.
Menu entries Encrypt 1 to Password 6, Self-test 7, Help 8, as the README table and xtask/src/terminal_texts.rs.
AUD-048-DOC001: help and the decrypt passphrase question name mhfe new.
on_stop_signals lives in protect.rs and shares handle() with interrupt_on_quit_and_suspend; terminal.rs chooses per platform; the Mach-O tool is self-contained in xtask.
AUD-048-ARC003 and AUD-048-ARC004.
AUD-048-ARC001, AUD-048-ARC002 and AUD-048-ARC005.
Feature gates consistent apart from AUD-048-ARC003; ctrlc moved to the Windows target; the per-module wasm clippy loop passed.
Six archives by default; the release workflow runs the canonical macOS programs on macOS, self-test and terminal suite, Intel through Rosetta 2.
Cargo.lock changes only the version; Zig is pinned by SHA-256 and cargo-zigbuild by version with --locked; the notices drop exactly the six crates; AUD-048-BLD002.

Zig and cargo-zigbuild are fetched only in the toolchain stage; the macOS builds run without network and with the builder paths remapped and checked; two builds in different environments give the same macOS archives.
The macos job needs the canonical one, publish needs all four, and canonical.sha256 covers all six archives against the files received.
AUD-048-DOC001, AUD-048-DOC002 and AUD-048-DOC004.
Every relative link and anchor resolves; 76 documented commands parse; AUD-048-DOC003 and AUD-048-DOC005.
No audit record changed since 8a15bed.

findings.title: The program's help and the decrypt passphrase question still name the removed mhfe new
findings.reproduction: mhfe check --help (the --words help) and an interactive mhfe decrypt of a 24-word container, which shows check::SOURCE_CHECK_WHY before the passphrase question.
findings.expected: The 0.8.0 program names no command it does not have; a 24-word phrase drawn to pass the check is described without a command.
findings.observed: '... drawn with the phrase + passphrase check of mhfe new.' and '... as mhfe new offers.'; both strings are in the release binary, and mhfe new is an unknown command.
findings.impact: A person is sent to a command the program refuses; no secret or result is affected.
findings.evidence: Both reviewers read the sources; reviewer B found both strings in the built release binary. No terminal case pins these texts.
findings.recommendedFix: Reword words_help() and SOURCE_CHECK_WHY without mhfe new, keeping SOURCE_CHECK_WHY within choice::fits.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo test check::tests; strings of the release binary hold no 'mhfe new'; cargo xtask terminal.

findings.title: docs/CLI.md shows the hidden menu-only option mhfe password --repeat as a command

findings.observed: A hidden option of the start menu is offered as an example; without a terminal it fails.

findings.title: cargo xtask macos-binary panics on, or mishandles, code directories outside its assumptions
findings.reproduction: By reading rehash_pages: a page-size byte of 64 or more overflows the shift; a code limit beyond the file or more code slots than pages make the slice panic; slot * page can overflow; a page-size byte of 0 hashes 1-byte pages; nothing checks that the code directory lies inside the signature, that the code limit ends before the signature, or that LC_UUID's size covers 16 bytes.
findings.expected: Every field out of range or unsupported is refused with the tool's error.
findings.observed: Panics, or a silently wrong signature for a page-size byte of 0; no test covers a program without a signature.
findings.impact: Bounded: the input is the project's own Zig output inside the reproducible build, and the result runs on a Mac in the release workflow.
findings.evidence: Reviewer A, by reading against the CodeDirectory layout; confirmed by the coordinator.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse each case and use checked arithmetic and get() for page slices; add tests for a program without a signature and for each refusal.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo test -p xtask; two canonical builds give the same macOS archives.

findings.title: Zig links its own compiler-rt into the macOS programs, and the notices do not name Zig
findings.reproduction: zig cc -target aarch64-macos.11.0 h.c -nodefaultlibs -lSystem -v: the link line ends with Zig's libcompiler_rt.a, also with -nodefaultlibs as rustc passes it.
findings.expected: Every archive names the licence of any code linked into its program, or it is shown that none is.
findings.observed: The macOS programs are stripped, so it cannot be told whether a member of Zig's compiler-rt remains; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md does not name Zig.
findings.impact: A possible omission of an MIT notice in two archives; no functional effect.
findings.evidence: Reviewer B named the gap; the coordinator ran zig cc -v.
findings.recommendedFix: Name Zig's MIT licence in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for the macOS programs.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo xtask licences --check; the archives carry the notices.

findings.title: The package checks' stand-in worker still calls selfCheckWallet with a random source
findings.reproduction: servedByTheWebAssembly calls bindings.selfCheckWallet(tier, skip, random, onStart, onResult); the binding now takes (tier, skipIds, onStart, onResult).
findings.expected: The stand-in serves the wallet self-check as web/wallet-worker.js does.
findings.observed: random lands in onStart and onStart in onResult: the binding swallows the failed call and no per-part message is posted; the checks pass because they assert only the final report.
findings.impact: Test fidelity only: a wrong argument order to a raw self-check binding goes unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Reviewer A read classes.js, src/wasm_api/wallet.rs and the generated glue.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the random argument and assert the wallet's per-part progress.
findings.requiredVerification: cargo xtask package-check with an assertion that fails on the old call.
